 The truth about Bruno Guimaraes’ controversial move to Arsenal
 Hostile return awaits ex-Newcastle captain whose summer transfer saga was fanned by criticism in Brazil and a mysterious opening ‘offer’

 Published 
 21 November 2026 8:01am GMT
 Bruno Guimarães’s move to Arsenal was one of the most explosive transfers of the summer as Newcastle United ’s talisman and captain left a club where he was adored.
 As the Brazil international returns to St James’ Park on Saturday evening for the first time since completing his £75m switch in August, the circumstances around his controversial exit are brought back into focus.
 Guimarães hurt a lot of people when he forced his way out and while the wounds will heal in time given how brilliant the midfielder was for 4½ years, he can expect a hostile reception.
 The 29-year-old was a majestic player for Newcastle, but the way he conducted himself in the summer left supporters feeling betrayed. Telegraph Sport reveals for the first time the events leading up to his Arsenal move, what motivated it and what is behind his inconsistent start at the Emirates.
 Summer 2024 and reintegration
 To understand Guimarães’s state of mind you have to go back to 2024. He had been at Newcastle for 2½ years and endeared himself to everyone, but he had been open to leaving that summer.
 Having signed a new contract, he was well aware of the £100m release clause it included and convinced himself that one of Europe’s elite clubs would sign him.
 The Brazilian was the shining light in a team who had escaped relegation in his first season and qualified for the Champions League in his second. He was the best of the first influx of players after the Saudi Arabia takeover, joining from Lyon for £35m in January 2022.
 Guimaraes walks on to the St James’ Park pitch for the first time after completing his £35m transfer from Lyon in 2022
 Credit : Getty Images/Serena Taylor
 Telegraph Sport was told by senior figures at the time that Guimarães wanted to go, and with the club in danger of breaching profitability and sustainability rules his sale would solve their problem. That plan evaporated. Nobody was willing to activate the release clause or make a bid. Newcastle sold Elliot Anderson and Yankuba Minteh instead.
 Guimarães’s self-esteem took a hit. He had believed he was destined to play for one of Europe’s most powerful teams, but no club matching that description wanted him.
 Newcastle had finished seventh the previous season and Guimarães was not himself when he returned. Eddie Howe’s man-management was required to re-energise the player. He was given the captain’s armband, but started the campaign slowly.
 He was back to his best by the start of the winter and was superb in Newcastle’s triumphant League Cup-winning campaign. His love for the club, the city and supporters was genuine and his emotional post-match interview at Wembley, with tears streaming down his face, will go down in club folklore.
 "The fans deserve EVERYTHING... one of the best days of my life!" 🖤🤍
Bruno Guimaraes' emotional post-match interview after Newcastle win the Carabao Cup 🏆 https://t.co/nKWa60WAR5
— Sky Sports Football (@SkyFootball) March 16, 2025 
 When Newcastle finished that season qualifying for the Champions League for a second time, Guimarães was happy. When Alexander Isak announced he wanted to leave for Liverpool that summer, Guimarães was furious. Yet 12 months later, he would allow others, acting on his behalf, to resort to similar tactics.
 Isak doubled his wages at Liverpool and expected to challenge for the title and Champions League at Anfield. A seed was sown in the heads of several players. Guimarães was one of them.
 Project running out of steam
 While the likes of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali were poor last season as they considered life away from Newcastle, Guimarães’s standards remained high. He was excellent again and top goalscorer in the league.
 But in private Guimarães was growing more disgruntled. He had signed for a club who promised to win the Premier League and compete in the Champions League every season. Aged 28, he could see his retirement looming. He had a choice to make. Stay at Newcastle and play out the rest of his peak years at a club he loved. Or move to one that gave him a far better chance of winning the big prizes.
 As far as he was concerned, Newcastle were going backwards. The club were selling their best players and in his mind – a view shared by supporters and Howe – he was the most talented of all.
 Sandro Tonali (left) and Anthony Gordon both left Newcastle in the early stages of the summer window
 Credit : Getty Images/Serena Taylor
 If you were being kind, Guimarães started the summer willing to explore his options. In reality, he was desperate to get out and instructed his team to find a move. Howe had made it clear to him that the club did not want to sell, as had sporting director Ross Wilson, but Guimarães went to the World Cup with Brazil thinking his time as a Newcastle player was coming to an end.
 Brazilian criticism, negative perceptions and Howe’s exit
 Guimarães was well aware of the optics of demanding to leave. He had seen and felt the vitriol aimed at Isak after he went on strike. He wanted to avoid a similar fate, but that did not make him any less determined to depart.
 At the start of June, there was still hope a transfer could be avoided and that Guimarães would stay for one more season. There was even talk of a new contract to appease him.
 But the temptation to engineer an exit turned into conviction during the World Cup. At the centre of it, sources revealed, was how Guimarães was perceived in his homeland. There was a lack of respect and, what he felt, was a belittling of his form and achievements because he played for Newcastle.
 Guimarães felt he was unfairly criticised by the Brazilian media compared to other big-name stars who played for more prestigious clubs.
 When Brazil crashed out of the World Cup to Norway , that perception hardened. Guimarães, despite impressive displays, missed a penalty and felt the full force of the anger that followed Brazil’s early exit.
 HUGE SAVE 🫨
Bruno Guimaraes stutters, and Orjan Nyland is on the end of it; Brazil fail to capitalise on the penalty https://t.co/QVlvycKlAA
— ITV Football (@itvfootball) July 5, 2026 
 In his mind, he needed a new challenge. He wanted to compete for silverware and he wanted to be respected more in Brazil. A move to Arsenal would give him that.
 Howe was aware of Guimarães’s position and having been drained and wounded by the Isak saga 12 months earlier, emotions were raw. The two were extremely close and one of the many reasons behind Howe’s decision to quit was that he believed it was inevitable his captain would force his way out. Having already lost Gordon and Tonali, Newcastle were also going to lose their best midfielder and leader.
 In turn, when Howe quit, the last chance for Guimarães to change his mind vanished. Their fates were intertwined.
 Guimaraes had a close relationship with Eddie Howe
 Credit : Getty Images/Serena Taylor
 What really happened with Arsenal’s ‘multiple bids’?
 It was the saga of the summer, with constant reports and claims from so-called experts that Arsenal made multiple bids for Guimarães that were rejected by Newcastle.
 The truth can be revealed now. In July, Newcastle were shown a written offer from Arsenal by an intermediary. It was official looking, complete with Arsenal branding and said they would be willing to pay £45m for Newcastle’s captain.
 It was this document that was used to justify the constant stream of reports saying a bid had been made. Newcastle, though, were bemused. Not only was the fee offered derisory, but when they asked Arsenal to confirm the bid, they were greeted with silence for weeks.
 As a result, Newcastle dismissed it and maintained their “no bids” stance.
 It is believed by some well-placed sources that the document had been acquired to pacify Guimarães, who was angry about the lack of progress being made. His representatives wanted to prove to him that Arsenal’s interest was genuine and they were working hard on his behalf. However, it was the key part of a tactic to feed into media pressure on Newcastle to sell.
 Speculation about Guimaraes’ Newcastle future continued while the midfielder represented Brazil at the World Cup during the summer
 Credit : Getty Images/Elsa
 There were no direct conversations between the clubs until the end of July. Even then, Arsenal continued to discuss numbers around the £50m mark, adding performance-related add-ons which Newcastle told them were unacceptable.
 At the start of August, with Guimarães’s return to pre-season training looming and growing concern he could stay away, Newcastle issued an ultimatum. They would accept an offer of £75m paid in full, with no clauses. If Arsenal were not willing to pay it, Guimarães would not be sold. A deal was struck.
 An emotional farewell
 When Guimarães arrived late to Newcastle’s training camp in La Manga he knew the move was going to happen.
 There were some who accused the player of deliberately delaying his arrival to exert pressure on the Newcastle hierarchy, but by the time he arrived in Spain relationships were healthy.
 Guimarães had allowed others to do the groundwork to unsettle Newcastle and when he addressed the team before heading off for his medical at Arsenal, he paid an emotional tribute to the club, his team-mates and Howe.
 Guimarães burst into tears several times saying his goodbyes to staff and teammates. They respected his decision to leave. There was no lingering animosity towards him in the same way there had been for Isak.
 Matthias Jaissle tried to convince Bruno Guimaraes to stay at Newcastle - even when he was already set on joining Arsenal 👀 https://t.co/LHXiWZNUyQ
— Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) November 19, 2026 
 Guimarães had kept his hands clean. He had never publicly declared he wanted to go, but as one senior source told Telegraph Sport at the time: “If Bruno goes it will be down to one thing only, the force of his personality and his intense desire to leave… we do not want to lose him and have told his representatives all summer.”
 Assessing his early form at Arsenal
 Mikel Arteta was the driving force behind the pursuit. There were reservations from within the Arsenal leadership team. Nobody doubted Guimarães’s quality, but the £75m fee alarmed some.
 The player turned 29 this month and there were already signs at Newcastle last season that his physical output was dropping. In his defence, the sheer number of games played partly explains that. While his stamina had never been in doubt, Guimarães was not seen as a natural athlete. Newcastle worked diligently on his conditioning and fitness.
 The serious hamstring injury he suffered at the start of the year was Guimarães’s first long-term injury at Newcastle, but at his age they become harder to recover from.
 Arteta had no concerns and told people close to him that he believed Guimarães was a plug-in-and-play option who would be worth an extra 15 points a season at least.
 Mikel Arteta was resolute in his desire to bring Guimaraes to Arsenal
 Credit : PA/Agostino Gemito
 The Spaniard was locked into a “win-now” mentality. He did not want to worry about the long-term ramifications when there was an opportunity to build a dynasty at Arsenal. Retaining the Premier League title for the first time in the club’s history would cement his legacy. Nobody at the Emirates was in a position to argue against him.
 Guimarães was not fully fit when he signed and was protected by his new manager. A niggle limited his early minutes but Arteta believed Guimarães would help Arsenal get the ball forward quickly, with his ability to pass through the lines and take possession in tight spaces.
 Although he has only started four games out of 10 matches in the Premier League, they have all come in the last six. Despite some inconsistent displays, Arteta’s view about extra points already looks vindicated given Guimarães came off the bench to score the winners against Sunderland and Leeds United .
 Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀
📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max https://t.co/zQHSSLxC3o
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) September 12, 2026 
 There have been some misgivings too and Guimarães cannot be considered an automatic starter. He was particularly poor in the 3-0 defeat by Brighton and missed the crucial penalty in a Carabao Cup shoot-out upset by Fleetwood Town .
 When Guimarães does start, he has been taken off around the hour mark each time, which hints at a player still searching for peak physical form.
 Arteta has not been afraid to publicly challenge his summer signing. After he scored the winner against Leeds, Arteta was unrelenting, saying: “Every week, every game, every minute, every action, you have to be at that level. And at Brighton, he wasn’t… he can still be much better in the games and that’s what we have to demand.”
 It was a message repeated after a more impressive individual display against Hull City before the international break: “He’s much better, he had a massive impact, he’s hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That’s my conviction, I told him that in the dressing room – he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come.”
 There was always more to come from Guimarães in a Newcastle shirt. He was the club’s most important and revered player of the post-takeover era, but he abandoned them at a delicate moment, with the team in transition and in more need of his talent, leadership and talismanic quality than ever.
 That is why he will receive a toxic reception on Saturday night. He broke hearts and provoked anger amongst a fanbase that adored him. He sat back and watched his representatives agitate to get him out all summer because that was what he desperately wanted.
 The perception is, when the going got tough, he walked out and put his interests above everything else.
 In time, wounds will heal. When he stops playing for Arsenal, Guimarães will be given club-legend status. It is no more than he deserves. He is one of the finest players in Newcastle’s modern history. Whether he will be able to say the same at Arsenal remains to be seen.
